# Send an OTP

This recipe sends a six-digit login or sign-up code to a user's WhatsApp and checks it when they type it back. **Verification belongs to your app:** your backend generates the code, stores its hash with an expiry, counts attempts and decides when a resend is allowed, and open-wa only delivers the text with [`sendText`](/docs/reference/client/messages#sendtext). It works from any language through the Easy API, and there's an SDK version at the end.

## Before you start

- An Easy API session that is linked and ready. The [quick start](/docs/getting-started/quickstart) gets you there; `/health` should report `"connected": true`.
- A license on the sending number. Most OTP recipients have never chatted with your account, and starting a chat with a new number is a [licensed feature](/docs/licensing/licensed-features). Without one, the send fails with a license error.
- The user's phone number with its country code, for example `447700900123` for a UK number.

## Send the code

Generate the code with a secure random source, store only its hash with an expiry, then send it with `sendText`. The chat ID for a phone number is the digits followed by `@c.us`. A new request replaces any earlier code for that number, but only after a 60-second cooldown.

```js title="otp.mjs"
import { createHash, randomInt, timingSafeEqual } from 'node:crypto';

const OPEN_WA = 'http://127.0.0.1:8080';
const CODE_TTL_MS = 5 * 60_000;
const RESEND_AFTER_MS = 60_000;
const MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5;

// Use your database or Redis in production; a Map is enough to try it.
const pending = new Map();

const hash = (code) => createHash('sha256').update(code).digest();

export class ResendTooSoonError extends Error {
  constructor(waitMs) {
    super('Wait before requesting another code');
    this.retryAfterSeconds = Math.ceil(waitMs / 1000);
  }
}

export async function sendOtp(rawPhone) {
  const phone = rawPhone.replace(/\D/g, '');
  const previous = pending.get(phone);
  const wait = previous ? previous.sentAt + RESEND_AFTER_MS - Date.now() : 0;
  if (wait > 0) throw new ResendTooSoonError(wait);

  const code = String(randomInt(0, 1_000_000)).padStart(6, '0');
  pending.set(phone, { hash: hash(code), expiresAt: Date.now() + CODE_TTL_MS, sentAt: Date.now(), attempts: 0 });

  const response = await fetch(`${OPEN_WA}/api/messages/sendText`, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'X-API-Key': process.env.WA_API_KEY },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      to: `${phone}@c.us`,
      content: `${code} is your verification code. It expires in 5 minutes. Don't share it with anyone.`,
    }),
  });
  const body = await response.json();
  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(body.error ?? `open-wa returned ${response.status}`);
  return body.data; // the submitted message ID
}
```

A successful send returns the message ID:

```json
{ "success": true, "data": "true_447700900123@c.us_3EB0C7D5E4A1B2" }
```

The ID means WhatsApp accepted the message, not that the user has read it. Use [acknowledgements](/docs/guides/messages#acknowledgements) if you want to show "delivered" in your UI.

## Check the code

```js title="otp.mjs"
export function verifyOtp(rawPhone, code) {
  const phone = rawPhone.replace(/\D/g, '');
  const entry = pending.get(phone);
  if (!entry || Date.now() > entry.expiresAt) return false;
  if (++entry.attempts > MAX_ATTEMPTS) {
    pending.delete(phone);
    return false;
  }
  const ok = timingSafeEqual(entry.hash, hash(String(code).trim()));
  if (ok) pending.delete(phone);
  return ok;
}
```

Deleting the entry on success makes each code single-use, and the attempt limit stops guessing.

## Send and verify a code in your backend

Your app exposes two routes: one that sends a code and one that checks it. This Express example wraps the two functions above:

```js title="server.mjs"
import express from 'express';
import { sendOtp, verifyOtp, ResendTooSoonError } from './otp.mjs';

const app = express();
app.use(express.json());

app.post('/otp/request', async (req, res) => {
  try {
    await sendOtp(String(req.body.phone ?? ''));
    res.json({ sent: true, expiresInSeconds: 300, resendAfterSeconds: 60 });
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof ResendTooSoonError) {
      return res.status(429).json({ error: error.message, retryAfterSeconds: error.retryAfterSeconds });
    }
    console.error(error);
    res.status(502).json({ error: 'We could not send the code. Try again shortly.' });
  }
});

app.post('/otp/verify', (req, res) => {
  if (!verifyOtp(String(req.body.phone ?? ''), String(req.body.code ?? ''))) {
    return res.status(401).json({ verified: false });
  }
  // The number is verified: sign the user in or mark the number confirmed here.
  res.json({ verified: true });
});

app.listen(4000, () => console.log('OTP service on http://localhost:4000'));
```

Each rule lives in your backend:

- **Expiry.** A code works for five minutes. After that, `verifyOtp` returns `false` and the user has to ask for a new one.
- **Attempt limit.** After five wrong guesses the code is deleted, so a sixth try fails even with the right code.
- **Resend.** Send a new code only when the user taps a "Send a new code" button, and enable that button after `resendAfterSeconds`. The new code replaces the old one. Never resend automatically after a failed or uncertain send, because the first message may already be in the chat.
- **Success.** `/otp/verify` returns `{ "verified": true }` once, and the code can't be used again.

In production, keep `pending` in your database or Redis so codes survive a restart and work across several app instances, and rate-limit `/otp/request` per IP address as well as per phone number.

## Handle failed sends

| Response | What happened | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `503` with `API not available until the session is truly ready` | The session is starting or reconnecting. | Retry after a few seconds, or ask the user to try again shortly. |
| `500` with `Starting a chat with a new number requires an applied restricted or premium license.` | The number has no chat with your account and the session has no license. | Apply a [license](/docs/licensing/pricing). |
| `500` with `sendText could not confirm the result…` | The message may have been sent. | Don't resend automatically. Let the user ask for a new code after the cooldown; it replaces the old one. |
| `401` | The `X-API-Key` header doesn't match `WA_API_KEY`. | Send the same key the Easy API was started with. |

The 60-second cooldown and a per-IP limit stop abuse and keep your account's sending pattern normal; see [rate limits](/docs/operations/rate-limits).

## Offer a copy button

With a license applied, you can send the code as an interactive message with a copy button, so the user doesn't have to select the digits. Send it with [`sendInteractive`](/docs/reference/client/messages#sendinteractive) instead of `sendText`; [interactive messages](/docs/guides/interactive-messages) covers the other button types:

```js
await fetch(`${OPEN_WA}/api/messages/sendInteractive`, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'X-API-Key': process.env.WA_API_KEY },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    to: `${phone}@c.us`,
    content: {
      type: 'buttons',
      body: `${code} is your verification code. It expires in 5 minutes.`,
      actions: [{ type: 'copy', label: 'Copy code', code }],
    },
  }),
});
```

## With the SDK

If your backend runs in Node.js, start the session in-process with `create()` and call `sendText` directly. Failures throw a `SendTextError` with a `code` and an `outcome`; when `outcome` is `unknown`, the message may already have been sent.

```ts
import { create } from '@open-wa/wa-automate';

const client = await create({ sessionId: 'otp', licenseKey: process.env.WA_LICENSE_KEY });

try {
  await client.sendText(`${phone}@c.us`, `${code} is your verification code.`);
} catch (error) {
  if (error.code === 'LICENSE_REQUIRED') throw new Error('Apply a license to message new numbers');
  if (error.outcome === 'unknown') return; // don't resend; let the user request a new code
  throw error;
}
```
